description: A research report for the Washington State Department of Transportation (WA-RD 730.1, November 2009) by Anne Goodchild, Eric Jessup, Edward McCormack and colleagues on managing the freight system to limit the economic consequences of disruptions. Coverage: Washington State's highway, rail and related freight network. Methods: a review of resilience literature and practice, a GIS-based statewide freight transportation network model, detailed data collection for two industries, potatoes and diesel fuel, and analysis of how each responds to specific network disruptions such as corridor closures. Outcome: the potato sector is fragile and depends on the Interstate 90 corridor, while diesel distribution is highly resilient and not linked to I-90; the authors recommend adding origin-destination data for more sectors so WSDOT can rank closure strategies and improvements by economic impact. Format and access: free 171-page PDF. Licence and cost: free; no licence was stated. Caveats: 2009 data for two commodities only. Useful for network flow and resilience models of freight disruption at state level. It relates to the Freight Analysis Framework and the I-70 truck platooning case study in the catalogue.
